deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and the next: a space X with a closed subspace Y, the open complement X* = X \ Y, a 'tubular' neighbourhood V = V_{Y,X} of Y with V homotopy equivalent to Y (so Π1 V ≅ Π1 Y), and the deleted neighbourhood V* = V \ Y. The basic 'diagramme de groupoïdes' is Π1 X* <-i- Π1 V* -p-> Π1 V ≅ Π1 Y. When X*, Y and V* are connected, choosing base points gives the corresponding diagram of groups π1(X*) <- π1(V*) -> π1(Y), equation (10).

First claim (programmatic): one should be able to express not just π1 but the full homotopy type of X, or possibly of some stratified homotopy type attached to it, in terms of this diagram. Under asphericity hypotheses (vanishing of higher π_i of the pieces) this amounts to taking the homotopy pushout of the K(π,1)'s, a van Kampen–type statement. He says 'devrait pouvoir', so it is not proved.

Second claim, stated as clear and as holding without asphericity or normal local triviality: let 𝓕 be the full subcategory of sheaves of sets on X whose restrictions to X* and to Y are locally constant (i.e. constructible for the two-stratum stratification). Then 𝓕 is equivalent to the category of triples (17) (E_{X*}, E_{Y,X}; φ), where:
- E_{X*} is a local system on Π1 X*, i.e. an étale covering of X*;
- E_{Y,X} is a local system on Π1 V ≅ Π1 Y;
- φ is a morphism, not necessarily an isomorphism, of local systems on Π1 V*: (18) φ : p*E_{Y,X} -> i*E_{X*}.

The direction of φ is the specialization or 'exit' direction, from stalks on Y to stalks at nearby points of X*. This is the recollement description F <-> (F|X*, F|Y, F|Y -> i^*j_*(F|X*)) made purely combinatorial. Equivalently it is a functor on the exit-path category of the stratified space, written as a lax/comma-type diagram of groupoids.

On the next page, in the connected case, this becomes: a π1(X*)-set, a π1(Y)-set, and a π1(V*)-equivariant map between them, each regarded as a π1(V*)-set by restriction. The key example is a topological surface with Y a point a, where V* is the punctured disc D_a^*. This is the setting of tame ramification and of the Teichmüller tower of the Longue Marche/Esquisse. The purpose is the foundations of a theory of 'stratified topoi' and stratified homotopy types, aimed at Galois–Teichmüller and anabelian applications.
errors: The assertion that the equivalence holds 'indépendamment ... de locale trivialité normale' is too strong as stated. One needs some regularity (a conical or tubular neighbourhood structure, e.g. Whitney or tame stratifications) to ensure that V retracts onto Y compatibly with sheaves, and that stalks of F on Y are computed on V. Without this, sheaves locally constant on the strata need not be described by such data. Presumably this is implicit in the existence of V_{Y,X}.

The homotopy-type statement is only conjectural ('devrait pouvoir'). It holds as a homotopy pushout only under asphericity hypotheses on the pieces, or else requires higher (∞-)groupoids rather than groupoids.

ideas.what: Constructible sheaves for a two-stratum decomposition described as triples (local system on X*, local system on Y, non-invertible morphism of local systems on the deleted neighbourhood V*), i.e. as representations of a diagram of fundamental groupoids
ideas.modern_name: exit-path category / representations of the exit-path (stratified fundamental) groupoid; combinatorial recollement
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished); D. Treumann (2009); J. Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); J. Woolf; recollement from Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier (SGA4) and Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne
ideas.where_published: Recollement appears in SGA4 (Exposé IV). Stratified structures and dévissage are discussed programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). An explicit exit-path / groupoid formulation does not appear in his published texts to my knowledge.

ideas.what: The homotopy type of X (not only π1) should be determined by the diagram of groupoids Π1X* <- Π1V* -> Π1Y
ideas.modern_name: homotopy pushout / van Kampen for stratified spaces; stratified homotopy hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: Seifert–van Kampen, R. Brown (groupoid van Kampen); stratified homotopy theory of Quinn, Woolf, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Related themes in Esquisse d'un programme and Pursuing Stacks (1983).

ideas.what: Punctured infinitesimal disc D_a^* around a point of a surface as the local datum for a 'stratified' Galois theory of surfaces
ideas.modern_name: inertia/local monodromy at punctures; tame fundamental groupoid with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1, tame ramification; Esquisse); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame fundamental group); Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche (1981)

missed.claim: In 1981 Grothendieck explicitly describes constructible sheaves for a stratified space as functors on a diagram of fundamental groupoids, with a non-invertible specialization map φ on the deleted neighbourhood. This is essentially the exit-path description usually attributed to MacPherson (1990s) and Treumann/Lurie.
missed.quote: Cette catégorie 𝓕 est équivalente en effet à celle des systèmes (17) (E_{X*}, E_{Y,X}; φ) ... et φ un hom. de syst. locaux sur Π1 V*_{Y,X}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/historical point: the exit-path idea appears in Grothendieck's stratified-topos programme a decade before MacPherson. It is tied there to Galois–Teichmüller and anabelian goals, a linkage little explored in the exit-path literature.

missed.claim: Program: recover the full homotopy type of the stratified space (not only π1) from the diagram of groupoids, i.e. a stratified homotopy hypothesis.
missed.quote: on devrait pouvoir exprimer alors le type d'homotopie de X (et non seulement son π1) en termes du diagramme de groupoïdes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the stratified homotopy hypothesis (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine, Douteau–Waas), here motivated by applications to algebraic curves and surfaces.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard today (recollement / exit paths), but its explicit 1981 groupoid formulation by Grothendieck predates the usual credits. It is linked to his Teichmüller/anabelian programme, which is a moderately notable historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: '(18)' after 'diagramme de groupoïdes' is very likely '(8)', since (18) is the equation φ defined on the next page. The diagram of groupoids is presumably eq. (8), the analogue of the diagram of groups (10).
'en termes du diagramme δ' is likely 'diagramme (8)' (or '8,'), not a Greek delta. Likewise the superscript before 'catégorie' looks like '8)' rather than 'δ/'.
'type d'homotopie de 𝔷 X' — the symbol before X is probably a scribble or struck-out letter. The reading should likely be 'le type d'homotopie de X'.
'locale trivialité normale' is correct (normal local triviality).
Insertion '≅ Π1 Y' over Π1 V_{Y,X} is correct. The parenthesis reads '(comme rev. étale de Y)'.
